4. The learned Joint District, Judge while dismissing the suit observed that the suit is not maintainable, that the plaintiff had already received the running bills for the works done and that the plaintiff would be entitled to the money for the works done after proper measurement in accordance with tender documents. On appeal from the said judgment the High Court Division allowed the appeal and decreed the suit and declared that the plaintiff is entitled to get the bills against 7 groups D/1, D/2, E/1, E/2, E/3, F/1 and F/2 as per admission made by the defendant No. 1, the superintendent engineer, Dhaka National Housing Authority by his letter dated 8th January; 2003 exhibits-Jha to Jha(6) and accordingly, directed the defendants to prepare the bills against each group of works and to pay to the plaintiff within 30 days from date. 

 5. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned counsel appearing for the appellant contended that the High Court Division erred in law in decreeing the suit relying upon exhibit-Jha series in failing to consider that the plaintiff had already withdrawn the excess money against the works done in respect of groups D/1 , D/2, E/1, E/2, E/3, F/1 and E/2. In support of his contention Mr. Mahbubey Alam has taken us to the exhibits and the local investigation reports and submits that these reports have been managed by the plaintiff on an influencing the Commissioners which would be apparent from the reports and the tender documents. Mr. Mahbubey Alam contended that the learned Joint District Judge on a thorough consideration of the reports with the oral evidence on record rightly came to a definite finding that these reports are apparently perfunctory but the High Court Division without repelling those findings, abruptly decreed the suit relying upon exhibit-Jha series without considering that the plaintiffs had already received the money in advance against running bills-in respect of 7 groups and also had withdrawn the security money in collusion with the Officials of the appellants and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with. 

 12. Though the High Court Division was of the opinion that the reports are impartial and unbiased but decreed the suit relying upon the, letter of the defendant No. 1 dated 8th January, 2003 exhibit-Jha series. Thus the basis of the decree passed by the High Court Division is exhibits-Jha, Jha(1), Jha(2), Jha(3), Jha(4), Jha(5) and Jha(6). The High Court Division failed to notice that the learned Joint District Judge noticed these letters and observed that though the defendant No. 1 admitted in these letters that till June, 2002 the plaintiff did 72.83% works but that appendixes 2/3 and 2/4 of ex exhibits-Ga to Sa showed in accordance with these letters and as per claim of the plaintiff a descriptive sketch was filed which indicated that the plaintiff was given money on the basis of works done of Tk. 19,8,56,232/-. The High Court Division has totally overlooked the said finding. In this connection Mr. Mahbubey Alam drew our attention to the said appendixes which corroborated the findings of the learned Joint District Judge. Mr. M. Amirul Islam failed to give any reply as to whether the High Court Division adverted to the findings arrived at by the learned Joint District Judge. 

 16. As regards the first point raised by the learned counsel, we would like to observe that the High Court Division did not give any decree in respect of groups A, B and C. It gave decree in respect of 7 groups on the basis of admissions made by the defendant No. 1 in his letter dated 8th January, 2003 exhibit-Jha series. The work order for the 3 groups was given only on 18th December, 2002. This work orders were cancelled on 26th April, 2003 as admitted by Al-Haj Mizanur Rahman Mia (PW.1) in course of his cross-examination. Against which order, he instituted Writ Petition No. 3262 of 2003. This rule was discharged by judgment and order dated 15th March, 2006. The plaintiff got the work order in pursuance of an interim order made by the High Court Division in the above writ Petition and thereupon he did some earth works. The defendants asserted that they were compelled to give the work orders as per direction of the High Court Division in a contempt proceeding. The writ petition was ultimately discharged. In view of the above, whatever works the plaintiff did in respect of 3 groups are at their risks and perils.
